Subject: SIG -- Clarifications on data handling (retention / training)

Dylan,

Thanks for the initial SIG materials. A couple of items we need clarified before our internal review can proceed:

1) Prompt & inference logs: what fields are retained (timestamps, request/response text, token-level traces)? How long are logs kept in the hosted product by default?

2) Training on customer data: your SIG response mentioned "no customer data used for model training without consent" — can you confirm if any automated sampling or aggregation ever feeds back into model updates or quality datasets?

3) For customers who require zero retention, do you offer a configuration that prevents any request text from being written to persistent storage? If yes, how is that enforced and audited?

4) Any evidence we can include in our SOC 2 / SIG package (artifact IDs, diagrams, or statement) pointing at encryption-at-rest, key management, and access controls for logs?

We'd like a short response (one page) and any artifacts you can provide. Targeting our security review meeting on Thursday 4th.

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Lisa —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers are below; attached is a one-page answer doc (redwood_sig_answers_v1.pdf) and a data flow diagram for your package. If you'd like, Naomi (cc'd, our compliance lead) can hop on a quick call for any follow-ups.

1) Prompt & inference logs
- Fields retained: request metadata (timestamp, route, model version, client id), request/response text for full-text logging depending on configuration, and limited debug traces (no token-level secrets persisted by default).
- Default retention (hosted): 45 days. This is applied to full-text logs used for debugging and observability. Shorter retention windows can be configured per-account under our Hosted settings. Dedicated and Private deployments are customer-configurable and can be set to any retention they require by admin policy.

2) Training on customer data
- We do NOT use customer prompts or responses to train or fine-tune our shared models by default. There are two paths where model updates may incorporate signal: aggregated anonymized telemetry for system performance tuning (latency, failure rates) and opt-in programs where customers explicitly agree to share prompt/response data for model improvement. Any opt-in is governed by a written agreement and strict bounding (no PII allowed).

3) Zero-retention configuration
- Yes. Hosted customers can enable a "zero-persistence" flag which prevents request/response bodies from being written to persistent storage; only encrypted request metadata for billing/quotas is kept for 7 days in ephemeral caches for routing. For Dedicated/Private, administrators can enforce disk-level immutability to ensure no persistent logs are produced. We log these policy choices in our audit trail (see attachments).

4) Evidence & controls
- Attachments: redwood_sig_answers_v1.pdf (summary), data_flow_diagram.png (flows showing where data is stored/encrypted).
- Controls: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest with customer-managed KMS supported for Dedicated/Private, role-based access control (RBAC) for logs, and SOC 2 Type II scope for hosted control plane. We include an audit log for any engineer access to logs with justification fields.

Next steps: If you confirm which retention option you'd like (default-45d, custom-30d/7d, or zero-persistence), we can provide a signed statement and an updated artifact for your SIG packet before Thursday.

Best,

Lisa —

Following up with the three specific items and a short signed statement below. Naomi and Grace helped with the audit examples.

- Aggregated telemetry: raw prompt text is NOT included in the aggregated telemetry stream used for system performance/latency analysis. Aggregation is performed over a 24-hour window and aggregates counters/percentiles (e.g., p50/p95 latency) and error rate signals. Any textual artifacts are hashed and truncated for debugging only and are retained only when a debug flag is active for a running incident (and then purged per the retention policy).

- Zero-persistence & cloud backups: the zero-persistence flag routes request/response bodies to an in-memory path that never touches durable block storage. We disable snapshot agents for the service instance and mark volumes as ephemeral; for hosted customers we operate an isolated path that is never included in scheduled backups. Documentation for this configuration and the administrative checklist is included in the attached PDF and in our compliance portal (link below).

- Audit sample (redacted):
  - timestamp: 2026-09-21T08:22:13Z | user: eng_ops_jdoe | action: VIEW_INFERENCE_LOG | target: acct-ACM-1234/req-9b3f | justification: "investigating elevated error rate on route v2"
